claims.text: The initial homogenized, cast TaNbHfZrTi-based alloy has a disordered BCC matrix.
Adding 2–3 at.% Al and aging near 900–1000°C for 2 hours followed by quenching will produce B2 precipitates in the TaNbHfZrTi-based alloy.
The resulting B2 precipitates will be uniformly dispersed, nanoscale, and coherent within the disordered BCC matrix.
Al addition reduces the density of the TaNbHfZrTi-based alloy.
The nanoscale precipitates obstruct dislocation motion through Orowan looping.
Orowan strengthening by the B2 precipitates remains effective around 800°C.
A continuous ductile BCC matrix containing discrete B2 precipitates can provide a balance of strength and room-temperature ductility.
The proposed Al addition and aging treatment will preserve room-temperature ductility in the TaNbHfZrTi-based alloy.
The proposed alloy will achieve at least twice the high-temperature yield strength of the untreated baseline around 800°C.
The proposed treatment will have minimal impact on alloy density relative to the untreated baseline.
Keeping the Al content within 2–3 at.% is necessary to obtain the anticipated benefits.
Keeping the aging treatment near 900–1000°C is necessary to obtain the anticipated benefits.
Departures from the proposed Al range or aging window may cause excessive precipitate coarsening or deleterious phase formation.
Excessive precipitate coarsening or deleterious phase formation would reduce ductility.
Precipitation strengthening is an established strengthening mechanism in high-entropy alloys.

contradictions.description: The stated baseline lacks both Al addition and controlled aging, but the experiment ages all samples, including the 0% Al control. Thus the experimental control does not reproduce the stated untreated baseline and cannot directly test the claimed combined intervention against that baseline.
